Article Title: How far will Jerry Jones go to punish Donovan Ezeiruaku? Cowboys’ $500K fine after Saints Brawl raises questions
Article Text:
How far will Jerry Jones go to punish Donovan Ezeiruaku? Cowboys’ $500K fine after Saints Brawl raises questions (Getty Images)

Jerry Jones confirms Donovan Ezeiruaku will face the Dallas Cowboys fine

Why Donovan Ezeiruaku’s second ejection has become a bigger concern?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jerry Jones is not letting Donovan Ezeiruaku walk away from the Cowboys-Saints brawl without consequences. The Dallas Cowboys owner plans to appeal the team’s $500,000 NFL fine, but he has also confirmed that players involved in the fights will receive fines from Dallas.Ezeiruaku stands out because Jones indicated he will be among those players fined. The second-year linebacker was ejected after throwing a punch at Saints center Erik McCoy, making this more than just another heated training-camp moment.Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has answered the biggest question surrounding Donovan Ezeiruaku. The Cowboys owner indicated that the young linebacker will receive a team fine after his role in the fight with New Orleans Saints center Erik McCoy.Jones spoke about the situation after the NFL fined the Cowboys and Saints $500,000 each for the repeated altercations during their joint practice. He made it clear that Dallas will handle the players separately from the league’s punishment.“I think that you have to have consequences, and that needs to register,” Jones said while speaking to reporters in Oxnard after the Cowboys completed their final training-camp practice there.He added that players need to understand the consequences of their behavior.That directly answers how far Jones plans to go with Ezeiruaku. The Cowboys will not simply accept the NFL fine and move forward. The team will also take money from the players responsible for the incidents.Jones has not announced the exact amount Ezeiruaku will pay. However, he indicated that Ezeiruaku is one of the Cowboys players who will receive a fine.The punishment comes after a chaotic joint practice that featured several fights between Dallas and New Orleans. Players from both sides exchanged punches, joined confrontations away from their original practice fields and pushed the session close to cancellation.The Cowboys and Saints coaches had to discuss whether they should end the practice early. Schottenheimer later said the session became too “chippy” and admitted that the teams did not get enough of the work they wanted.Ezeiruaku became one of the most visible Cowboys players in the chaos. He got into it with McCoy and threw a punch, leading officials to eject him.The bigger concern for Dallas is that this was his second ejection for throwing a punch during training camp. That makes the internal fine more than a simple response to one bad moment. The Cowboys now need Ezeiruaku to show that he can control his emotions while keeping the physical edge they want from him.Schottenheimer had already dealt with Ezeiruaku after his earlier ejection. The Cowboys coach again addressed the young defender after the Saints practice and stressed that Ezeiruaku cannot hurt the team by losing his composure.Speaking after the practice, Schottenheimer called Ezeiruaku a “very bright young man” and said he understands that he cannot hurt the football team. The coach also described the incident as part of a “growth mindset” and said Dallas has leaders who can help him improve.The message from Schottenheimer and Jones is similar. Dallas does not want to remove Ezeiruaku’s aggression. The Cowboys want him to know when that aggression has gone too far.That is especially important because Ezeiruaku has a meaningful role to play on the Dallas defense. He started nine games as a rookie and recorded two sacks, giving the Cowboys reason to continue developing him as part of their pass rush.The Cowboys therefore have no reason to give up on him over a pair of training-camp incidents. But they also cannot ignore repeated punches, especially when the latest incident helped turn a joint practice into a league disciplinary issue.The NFL fined Dallas and New Orleans $500,000 each after reviewing the fights. The league reminded teams that they must prevent unsportsmanlike behavior at joint practices, particularly conduct that could cause injuries.Jones called Dallas’ fine “pretty stiff” and said the Cowboys will appeal. He still understands why the league wants teams to control these situations.That creates two separate consequences for Ezeiruaku’s team. The Cowboys will challenge the $500,000 organizational fine, while Ezeiruaku and other players involved will pay separate fines to Dallas.The Cowboys have not revealed Ezeiruaku’s exact penalty. For now, Jones has made the main point clear: the linebacker will face a financial consequence, and the team expects him to learn from it.For Ezeiruaku, the next step is on the field. The Cowboys still want his physical style and pass-rush ability. They simply need him to keep his punches out of the equation.
Article Summary: Jerry jones confirms donovan ezeiruaku will face the dallas cowboys fine. Second-year linebacker was ejected after throwing a punch at saints center erik mccoy. Nfl fined the cowboys and saints $500,000 each for the repeated altercations. The cowboys will challenge the $500,000 organizational fine.

Article Title: Luka Doncic gives first Lakers roster outlook after spending $18,000 an hour flight for teammates: See Photos
Article Text:
Luka Doncic. Image via: Adam Pantozzi/ NBAE via Getty Images

Luka Doncic gives first Lakers roster outlook in LeBron James-less era

Luka Doncic shares a teammate's photo. Image via: Luka Doncic/ Instagram

Luka Doncic reportedly spent $18,000 an hour for teammates

The Lakers are building the roster around Doncic

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Luka Doncic has made his first major statement as the undisputed face of the Los Angeles Lakers. With LeBron James gone after joining the Philadelphia 76ers, Doncic brought the Lakers to Slovenia for a four-day minicamp designed to build chemistry before his first full season as the franchise's centerpiece. He welcomed his teammates with dinner, workouts, pickup games, golf and time exploring Ljubljana, turning an offseason trip into an early test of his leadership.The itinerary mixed basketball with leisure. The players worked out, played pickup games, visited Lake Bled for fishing, played golf and explored Ljubljana. Dinner at Doncic's favorite restaurant was also part of the trip.Doncic's Instagram Story captured the start of the gathering with a simple caption: “First supper,” Doncic wrote.The Lakers enter the 2026-27 season with Doncic at the center of everything. James' departure ended a defining chapter in Los Angeles, while Doncic's first full season as the team's unquestioned leader begins with a roster built around his offensive game.Doncic's production gives the Lakers plenty to build on. He led the league with 33.5 points per game in 2025-26 while averaging 8.3 assists, 7.7 rebounds and 1.6 steals.He shot 47.6% from the field and 36.6% from 3-point range.Los Angeles also made significant moves around him. The Lakers retained Austin Reaves on a four-year, $185 million contract and acquired Walker Kessler from the Utah Jazz through a sign-and-trade. Kessler received a four-year, $130 million deal, while the Lakers also sent two unprotected first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps in the transaction.Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Kevon Looney, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams were among the other additions. It appears that the Lakers are constructing a roster intended to maximize Doncic's strengths.The trip also came with a remarkable price tag. Doncic reportedly chartered a Bombardier Global 8000 for 14 Lakers players, with the 13-hour flight costing at least $18,000 per hour. The 26-hour round trip is expected to cost roughly $500,000, according to Slovenian outlet 24ur.com, with Doncic covering the expense.Doncic's leadership has not been limited to roster decisions. The Slovenia trip gave him a chance to create the kind of shared experience that can be difficult to manufacture during an NBA season.The 14 players reportedly traveled aboard a luxurious Bombardier Global 8000. Images from the flight showed a lounge area, individual bedrooms, beds, couches, recliners and televisions. After arriving, Doncic met his teammates alongside his daughter, Gabriela.The Lakers need their new hierarchy to work on the court, but Doncic also needs to establish himself inside a locker room that previously revolved around James.This is not Doncic's first attempt at bringing his teammates together. He organized a Porsche Driving Experience for the Lakers in October 2025, shortly after joining the organization.This minicamp carries more weight. James is no longer there, and Doncic now enters the season without another established superstar occupying the franchise's leadership role.The Lakers are also dealing with significant organizational change. Mark Walter's $12.5 billion purchase of the team and the Buss family's dispute over its remaining stakes have added another layer of uncertainty around the franchise.Doncic has so far handled that backdrop while remaining focused on basketball. The Slovenia minicamp gives him an opportunity to set the tone before training camp and the regular season arrive.
Article Summary: Luka doncic took the lakers to slovenia for a four-day minicamp. The trip included dinner, workouts, pickup games, golf and time exploring ljubljana. The lakers are building the roster around doncick's offensive game.

Article Title: "I try to be the connector": Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry open up about their equal partnership in charity work
Article Text:
Stephen Curry shares.(Image via Getty Images)

Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry explain how the two divide their work equally when it comes to their charity

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Stephen Curry focuses on recovery amid concerns over his fitness ahead of the new season

Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have always been a team even though their marriage has been surrounded by a number of negative rumors throughout the last decade. Despite the negative drama, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have remained united in all their efforts.A few weeks ago, in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter, Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry opened up about her work and department in their foundation, Eat. Play. Live, as she said, “I feel like I’m the big-ideas girl. I always have big, loud ideas that I want to accomplish now — or yesterday. The hardest thing for me, personally, has been reeling back a bit to come to the understanding that baby steps are important. ”The four time NBA champion Stephen Curry also opened up about his area of work as he added, “I try to be the connector, especially when we’re reaching out to our network. We’re building a family, in a sense, of people who, again, believe in our mission and want to commit time and resources, whether that be financial or otherwise.”The Golden State Warriors’ star player continued, “When I’m on the court, I want people to enjoy the way that I played…I want them to feel something and be inspired to achieve greatness in whatever they decide to do.Family-wise, we want to have a cohort of hopefully thousands of kids whose lives have been impacted because of the work that we’ve done. We don’t need a parade for that. It’s who we are.”Both the four time NBA champion Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have remained dedicated towards building their foundation, Eat. Learn and Play, throughout the last decade.Eat. Learn and Play has actively worked for underprivileged children and families in Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s hometown, Oakland.Throughout the last decade, the team has actively worked for over 10,000 children and has looked after their food and provided quality education.Both Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry have handled their busy professional and personal lives while they have actively worked towards the children in Oakland.Ahead of the new season, there have been many concerns about Stephen Curry’s fitness after he ended up sustaining a patellofemoral pain syndrome (runner's knee) and bone bruising in his right knee which kept him out of court for two months.Even though the NBA legend could come back for his team, Stephen Curry has kept his full focus on complete recovery during the offseason.With the Golden State Warriors scheduled to play a demanding season, many remain stressed about him.
Article Summary: Stephen curry and his wife, ayesha curry, have always been a team even though their marriage has been surrounded by a number of negative rumors throughout the last decade. The four time nba champion stephen curry has remained dedicated towards building their foundation, eat. Learn and play.

Article Title: South Middle School football game halted after 16-year-old girl ‘attacks’ player, faces assault and disorderly conduct charges
Article Text:
South Middle School football game halted after 16-year-old girl ‘attacks’ player, faces assault and disorderly conduct charges

16-year-old girl tackles South Middle School football player

South Middle School football game ends early after field incident

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A 16-year-old girl is facing assault and disorderly conduct charges after she ran onto the field during a middle school football game in Winchester, Tennessee, and tackled a South Middle School player. The incident happened Tuesday night during the game against Cornersville Middle School at Franklin County High School. Game officials stopped the game and the stadium was cleared. No injuries were reported, according to WSMV and the Franklin County Sheriff’s Office.The incident began after South Middle School scored a touchdown and an extra point. According to WSMV, a scuffle then started between two players from the teams. Investigators said the 16-year-old girl, who is from Marshall County, ran onto the field and went straight toward the South Middle School player involved in that exchange.Video from the game shows the girl coming from the stands and making contact with the player, sending both to the ground. The player got back up, but the girl pushed him down again. A person who appeared to be a coach then stepped in and stopped the confrontation.The girl left the field afterward, but a school resource officer met her as she was leaving. She was later released to her parents, who were at the game. The Franklin County Sheriff’s Office said she was charged with assault and disorderly conduct.The reason she ran onto the field has not been confirmed by authorities. Reports only connect her actions to the scuffle that followed South Middle School’s touchdown. There is no official information showing what, if anything, happened between the girl and the player before she entered the field.Referees ended the game after the girl entered the field. Officials cleared the playing area and then emptied the stadium. The game between South Middle School and Cornersville Middle School did not continue.NewsChannel 5 reported that no one was injured in the incident. The Franklin County Sheriff’s Office also confirmed that the girl was released to her parents after she was taken into custody.The school consequences are also serious. Franklin County Schools issued a lifetime ban keeping the girl off all district properties. The Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association separately banned her from attending Cornersville Middle School home and away athletic events for one year.The game was played at Franklin County High School because South uses that venue for home games. The Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association confirmed the one-year event ban. The incident was captured on video and circulated in reports about the game.WSMV reported that South Middle School’s principal praised the staff, coaches and school resource officers for how they handled the situation.The girl’s identity has not been made public because she is 16. The available reports do not say whether she has a lawyer or give further details about the juvenile case. Authorities have not publicly stated what led to the confrontation beyond the scuffle involving the players.
Article Summary: A 16-year-old girl is facing assault and disorderly conduct charges after she ran onto the field during a middle school football game in winchester, tennessee. The incident happened tuesday night during the game against cornersville middle school at franklin county high school.

Article Title: Inspiring story on motherhood: "It's probably the hardest thing I've ever done in my life...it's the most daunting task" - How Donna Kelce navigated the challenges of raising Jason and Travis Kelce
Article Text:
Jason Kelce, Donna Kelce and Travis Kelce (Getty Images)

Donna Kelce’s powerful words about motherhood

Glamour group interview published on October 3, 2024

Raising Jason and Travis Kelce was never just about football

Donna Kelce was also building a career

The values behind Jason and Travis Kelce’s success

Why Donna Kelce’s motherhood confession still resonates

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Donna Kelce, motherhood was never simply about getting her children through childhood. It meant working hard, making difficult choices and giving Jason and Travis Kelce the freedom to discover who they were. Years before they became NFL stars, she was a working mother trying to keep family life steady. In 2024, she opened up about just how demanding that journey had been.Donna Kelce shared her candid thoughts on motherhood during a. The conversation was part of Glamour’s 2024 Women of the Year feature, which brought together Donna, Tina Knowles, Maggie Baird and Mandy Teefey to discuss raising children who would eventually become major figures in sports, music and entertainment.Asked about what motherhood had been like for her, Donna did not describe it as an effortless or glamorous experience. Instead, she focused on the responsibility that comes with raising children who depend on you for almost everything.She said:“Being a mom is probably the hardest thing I’ve ever done in my life. It’s so much easier to just go to work.”Donna Kelce then explained that raising children means trying to make the best choices possible while dealing with limited resources and the constant responsibility of caring for people who rely on you.She ultimately described motherhood as the most daunting task she had ever taken on.The honesty in her answer is striking because it came from someone whose sons would later become two of the most recognizable names in American football. Yet Donna was not talking about fame when she made the comment. She was talking about the everyday work of being a mother.That distinction matters.Jason and Travis Kelce did not begin their childhoods with a clear path toward professional football. Donna told Glamour that the brothers tried several sports, including hockey, lacrosse and basketball. Football came later, when they reached seventh grade.Even then, Donna did not immediately know that her sons would build professional careers from the sport.She said the possibility became clearer only when college recruiting letters began arriving. Until that point, she was simply watching two athletic boys grow, compete and find interests of their own.That detail gives her motherhood comments more weight.The woman who eventually became known around the NFL as “Mama Kelce” was not raising two guaranteed stars. She was raising children without knowing where their talents would eventually take them. Her job was to give them room to grow while keeping them grounded.Donna has also spoken about the energetic nature of her sons as children. During the same Glamour conversation, she recalled broken windows and calls from neighbors, while making clear that Jason and Travis were not bad children. They were simply energetic and, as she put it, rambunctious.Those memories offer a very different picture from the polished image fans now see.Before the Super Bowl appearances, championship celebrations and packed stadiums, there were ordinary family moments. There were mistakes, sports practices, neighborhood adventures and the countless small responsibilities that come with raising children.Another important part of Donna’s story is that motherhood did not happen in isolation.She was also working.Donna had a career in banking and later described herself as a major breadwinner in her family. She told Glamour that she worked extremely hard because she wanted to move forward professionally. At the same time, she believed it was important for her children to see that a woman could build a career and pursue her own ambitions.That balance adds another layer to her comments about motherhood.For Donna, going to work could be demanding, but parenting carried a different kind of responsibility. A job has defined duties, deadlines and hours. Raising children is far less predictable. It follows you home. It changes as children grow. And there is no simple measure for whether you are doing it right.Her reflections also touched on her marriage to Ed Kelce. Donna said the couple knew their marriage was no longer working but chose to remain together for their children for a period of time. She described their relationship as friendly and said they wanted to keep life as normal as possible for Jason and Travis.Eventually, Donna said she had to move forward on her own.That part of her story shows that her definition of motherhood was not limited to the visible moments. It included personal sacrifices and decisions that her sons may not have fully understood while they were growing up.Donna Kelce’s influence becomes easier to understand when looking at how she talks about her sons today.She has consistently emphasized supporting children rather than forcing them into a particular future. In the Glamour interview, she explained that parents learn more about their children as they encounter people and experiences outside their immediate community. Her approach was to support what her children loved and encourage them to enjoy it.That philosophy appears to have shaped the Kelce family.Jason eventually became a Super Bowl champion with the Philadelphia Eagles and one of the most respected centers of his generation. Travis established himself as one of the NFL’s premier tight ends with the Kansas City Chiefs.Their achievements are enormous. But Donna's comments suggest that she measures success differently.For her, keeping her sons grounded mattered just as much as celebrating their accomplishments.She told Glamour that she would remind Jason and Travis of their childhood when fame became overwhelming. The goal was simple: remind them where they came from and help them remember that they were still the same people they had always been.That perspective became especially meaningful as both brothers entered a world where almost every part of their lives could attract public attention.Donna Kelce’s description of motherhood stands out because it cuts through the glamour surrounding her family.Today, Jason and Travis are household names. Their games attract millions of viewers, their personal lives generate constant headlines and their family has become part of the wider sports conversation.But Donna’s story began somewhere much quieter.It began with a mother working, raising two boys and trying to make good decisions without knowing exactly where those decisions would lead.Her statement to Glamour was powerful because she did not present motherhood as a perfect journey. She acknowledged the pressure, uncertainty and sacrifice involved. She also recognized that the work of raising children often happens without applause.That may be the most revealing part of her story.The world sees the Super Bowl rings, the records and the stadium lights. Donna remembers the years before all of that. She remembers the children who needed her, the choices she had to make and the effort required to help them become independent adults.Her famous sons may now be the stars, but Donna’s words offer a reminder that behind many extraordinary careers is a much more ordinary story: a parent showing up, day after day, and doing the best they can.And for Donna Kelce, that was the hardest job of all.
Article Summary: Donna kelce said motherhood is the hardest thing she's ever done in her life. Jason and travis kelce did not begin their childhoods with a clear path toward professional football. Donna did not immediately know that her sons would build professional careers from the sport.

Article Title: After Jaspal Rana’s sudden demise, Paris Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker forging new bonds with Serbian coach
Article Text:
Manu Bhaker with her new coach (Photo by Jelena Arunovic)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BHOPAL: After adjusting the lighting at the MP State Shooting Academy final hall, two young electricians asked Manu Bhaker if she needed anything else. “Nahin,” the shooting star politely replied. The electricians were still waiting. Distracted, Manu suddenly realized it hadn’t hit home, and gave them a thumbs up with a smile.Job well done, the men left the range content.With that stardom and popularity that surrounds her, the Paris Olympics double medallist may have realised at that moment, that a lot rides on her validation.Nearly a decade ago, in 2017, Manu, already a teenage star, was known to getting things done her way. Calling it stubbornness would perhaps be much; insistence on her plans, especially those concerning her sport, was her weapon. It was also the reason for her success.She has a different weapon now -- flexibility. While a certain doggedness suited her teenage self, flexibility is becoming of a mature Manu.Other than being a good judge of situations, Manu is also mastering the art of changing according to its demands.After the sudden passing away of her coach, Jaspal Rana, two months back, Manu has adapted herself with Serbian coach Jelena Arunovic.The Indian star, attending the Asian Games camp here, has been spending over eight hours at the ranges. She reaches the range at 7.30 am and is the last to leave with Jelena late afternoon. In between, some intense training happens.“Her openness to new methodologies has definitely made the transition to a slightly different way of working easier,” Jelena told TOI.“I think her flexibility comes first from the fact that she is never completely satisfied with her current level. She is always looking for what can still be improved, either to achieve a better result or to make her performance more stable. That is actually a trait of top athletes,” she added.The shooter is forging a bond with her new coach, spends hours with her at the ranges, and follows the unconventional ways of training that the Serbian brings. The 24-year-old does all this, without fuss or frown.“I think flexibility at this level does not mean accepting every change immediately. It means being able to understand why something is being changed, test it seriously, and then see whether it can actually help your performance,” Jelena, who had coached her sister Zorana to a gold in Paris, said.It isn’t just about training under a new coach. It is also about training with different ideas and different philosophies. With less than two years left for the 2028 LA Games, the star of 2024 looks in no mood for complacency. She rather looks hungry for more and is doing everything to repeat her performance.
Article Summary: Manu bhaker has adapted herself with serbian coach jelena arunovic. The 24-year-old is forging a bond with her new coach, spends hours with her at the ranges. With less than two years left for the 2028 la games, the star of 2024 looks in no mood for complacency.

Article Title: Why referees are banned from speaking on TV at Real Madrid’s stadium despite La Liga’s new transparency protocol
Article Text:
Real Madrid president Florentino Perez gives a press conference in Madrid, Tuesday, May 12, 2026. (AP Photo/Bernat Armangue)

What is La Liga's new refereeing protocol?

Referee shows a yellow card to Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe during a Spanish La Liga soccer match between Real Madrid and Girona in Madrid, Spain, Friday, April 10, 2026. (AP Photo/Manu Fernandez)

Why is the Bernabéu the exception?

A problem rooted in Real Madrid's tense relationship with La Liga

What will fans see elsewhere?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

La Liga has introduced a new refereeing protocol designed to give supporters more insight into how key decisions are made, with officials now able to speak on television about important incidents. But there is one notable exception to the new system: Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabéu.Referees will be able to give pre-match and post-match interviews at La Liga stadiums when requested by broadcasters, as well as explain the most significant decisions and incidents from games. The Bernabéu is the only one of La Liga’s 20 stadiums where the protocol cannot be used, because Real Madrid’s restrictions on broadcasters’ connections prevent the interviews from taking place. At every other venue, referees will be available to speak before and after matches.The policy marks a significant change from the traditional approach of referees remaining largely silent when it comes to explaining their decisions.The first referee interventions were heard during the opening round of La Liga, while the system is due to expand from Matchday 10. From that point, referees will be able to speak before and after matches when broadcasters request interviews, and they can also be asked about the most notable incidents from the game.The Spanish refereeing body has stressed that officials will speak in stadiums “where the necessary conditions for this are available”, while insisting there is no distinction between clubs or grounds.That means the intention is for supporters around Spain to hear referees explain some of the decisions that can otherwise leave fans debating what happened and why.The Santiago Bernabéu is the only La Liga stadium excluded from the new system, according to Catalan newspaper Sport The reason is not that the refereeing committee has specifically banned Real Madrid from participating, nor is there a separate rule targeting the club. Instead, it comes down to the broadcasting arrangements at the stadium.Real Madrid restricts broadcasters' connections from the Bernabéu, allowing them to be established only a few minutes before kick-off. Those restrictions prevent broadcasters from creating the connections needed for the referee interviews to take place under the new protocol.In practical terms, referees can speak at other stadiums because the necessary broadcast infrastructure and connections can be arranged. At the Bernabéu, the existing restrictions make that impossible.The broadcasting restrictions come against the backdrop of an already strained relationship between Real Madrid and both La Liga and the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF).That tension has also affected the conditions under which broadcasters operate from the Bernabéu. Real Madrid, under president Florentino Pérez, maintains restrictions on when broadcasters can establish their connections from the stadium, and those conditions now have a direct impact on the new refereeing transparency initiative.The refereeing body has made clear that this is not a decision by its officials to exclude Real Madrid. Its position is that referees will speak wherever the required conditions exist and that there is no discrimination between clubs or stadiums.From Matchday 10 onwards, supporters at other La Liga grounds will be able to hear referees speak before and after matches when broadcasters request their participation. Officials will also be able to explain the most important decisions and incidents from the game.The measure is intended to provide greater transparency around refereeing decisions and give supporters a better understanding of why officials reached particular conclusions.The Bernabéu, however, will remain outside that system.So while the rest of La Liga moves towards giving fans more direct access to referees and their explanations, Real Madrid's home supporters will not have the same opportunity at their own stadium — not because referees have been instructed to stay silent there, but because of the broadcasting restrictions already in place at the Bernabéu.
Article Summary: La liga has introduced a new refereeing protocol designed to give supporters more insight into how key decisions are made. But there is one notable exception to the new system: real madrid’s santiago bernabéu. Referees will be able to give pre-match and post-match interviews at la liga stadiums when requested by broadcasters, as well as explain the most significant decisions and incidents from games.

Caitlin Clark’s Indiana Fever failed to survive against Paige Bueckers’ Dallas Wings. Bueckers and co. handed the Indiana Fever a 91-85 loss. The result ended Indiana's five-game winning streak, with Kelsey Mitchell's 37 points unable to prevent the Fever from falling on the road.The matchup featured two of the WNBA's biggest young stars, but it was Arike Ogunbowale and Jessica Shepard who made the bigger scoring impact for Dallas. Ogunbowale had 32 points, while Shepard added a career-high 26.The Dallas Wings held off the Indiana Fever 91-85, ending a five-game run that had pushed Indiana to 24-13. The Fever now travel to New York to face the Liberty on Saturday night.Indiana had to lean heavily on Mitchell, who scored 37 points and extended her remarkable streak to 21 consecutive games with at least 20 points, a new WNBA record. Aliyah Boston added 14 points and nine rebounds, while Makayla Timpson posted 11 points and 12 rebounds.Clark's nine assists were important in keeping Indiana's offense moving, but the Fever received little production beyond their main contributors. Indiana's bench scored only four points.Dallas had more balance. Ogunbowale's 32 points led all Wings scorers, while Shepard's 26-point performance marked a career high.Awak Kuier added 11 points, eight rebounds and seven blocked shots, giving Dallas a major defensive presence around the basket.The game was tied 42-42 at halftime. Clark had five points and six assists at the break, while Bueckers had five points. Shepard had already scored 22 for Dallas, and Kuier had six points along with five blocks.The game remained tight into the second half. Dallas led 61-56 with 1:29 left in the third quarter after Ogunbowale scored 12 straight points for the Wings. She eventually finished with 32, providing the late offensive push Dallas needed.Caitlin Clark scored 10 points in 35 minutes against Dallas, finishing with nine assists and four rebounds. She shot 4-for-15 from the field, including 2-for-8 from three-point range, and went 0-for-1 at the free-throw line.Clark also recorded one steal and one block, while committing three turnovers and four personal fouls. Her scoring was modest, but her nine assists reflected her continued role as one of Indiana's primary creators.Clark's presence has also remained a major factor beyond the court. The Fever's recent games have produced some of the WNBA's strongest television audiences.Indiana's Aug. 14 win over Dallas averaged 1.62 million viewers on ION, becoming the most-watched WNBA game in the network's history. The game peaked at 2.2 million viewers. Two days later, the Fever's overtime win over Atlanta averaged 2.58 million viewers on ESPN and peaked at 4 million.Paige Bueckers scored 13 points in 35 minutes, adding eight assists and six rebounds in the Wings' victory. Myles Gaskin announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 29 on Instagram . He had a tumultuous 2025 offseason and midseason.On August 10, 2025, he signed with the Baltimore Ravens. But on August 26, 2025, he was released during the final roster cuts. Later, in October 2025, he signed with the Seattle Seahawks’ practice squad. But on November 20, 2025, he was released. Wait, that’s not all.Six days later, the 29-year-old RB was re-signed by the Seahawks. And three days later, he was promoted to the active roster from the practice squad on November 29, 2025.But this to-and-fro, dicey situation did not stop there. Three days after joining the active roster, he was re-signed to the practice squad. Eventually, days later, the Seahawks released him on December 13, 2025. This team went on to win Super Bowl LX. This surely would have left a sour taste in Gaskin’s mouth.The whole dicey situation could make a player confused – Am I playing? Am I playing or not? Am I not playing? Am I still with the team? Have I left the team? Does the team still want me?Several people are involved in making decisions for a player, but when it comes to his retirement, only the player is involved.The whole dicey situation could have happened again in the 2026 offseason, but before Myles Gaskin could enter the “playing, not playing” madness, he gave up. Also, he remained unsigned by any NFL team until August 2026.The 29-year-old running back, who once recorded over 1,300 rushing yards on 220 carries and scored 14 touchdowns in college for the Washington Huskies, is no longer going to play professional football. He shared an emotional NFL retirement message through Instagram.Football gave Myles Gaskin the chance to fulfill his dream that was born long before the league stadiums, shiny lights, and Sunday crowds.He played seven seasons in the NFL. The journey took him from Richmond to O’Dea High School, the University of Washington, the Miami Dolphins, and finally, the Seattle Seahawks. He announced his NFL retirement through an emotional, gratitude-filled message on Instagram.“Thank you, God,” Gaskin wrote, reflecting on his childhood’s greatest dream that ultimately became his reality and allowed him to play the game he “loved at the highest level.”He thanked every stage of his football career that helped build him into the player – and the man – he became.He recalled his four years with the Washington Huskies, where he played “in the greatest setting in college football as a Dawg at the University of Washington.” He went back to his earlier days at O’Dea High School and as a Richmond Bulldog, tracing his path back to where the dream first began.His NFL journey brought him several memorable stops, starting with the Miami Dolphins and ending with the Seattle Seahawks.“To the Miami Dolphins, boy was that fun,” Gaskin wrote.But his final chapter carried a special meaning. The Seattle native was given the opportunity to play his last snaps back home with the Seahawks. “To the Seattle Seahawks, thank you for letting me play my last snaps back at the crib,” he said.Gaskin also paid tribute to the fans who make football what it is today, acknowledging the passion that fills the game from Friday nights and college Saturdays to NFL Sundays – and every other day football takes over the calendar.He later thanked every member of every team, stating, “To the staff, the organizations, my teammates, and coaches at every level, there are too many laughs, stories, and lessons to name, but every snap helped me grow into the man I always wanted to become.”The most emotional part of his goodbye message was reserved for the people who believed in him before the world even knew his name.Gaskin thanked longtime personal trainer, mentor, and CEO of Ford Sports Performance, Tracy Ford, for taking a chance on “a random kid” who walked into his gym, while also expressing gratitude to his older brother, Ivan Gaskin, for being the first person who ever believed in him.And then there were his parents, Scott and Robbie Gaskin.Gaskin credited them with giving him the freedom to chase his dream, the work ethic to pursue it and, most importantly, the support to do so without any peer pressure. “Thank you,” he wrote. “Couldn't have asked for better parents.”Although his playing days are over, Gaskin made it clear that his relationship with football is far from finished. Retirement won’t stop him.Unable to fully put into words what the game means to him, he promised to give back by helping the next generation of young players who dare to dream as he once did.After a journey defined by faith, family, and football, Myles Gaskin is walking away with immense gratitude. “Thank you,” he wrote. “It's been real. #MMFG #FFF – Faith, Family, Football. All glory to God.”PS: Myles Gaskin has not reportedly specified his reason for retirement at 29; instead, he expressed his wish to coach young football players.
